title: Does Orchestration Stay Scarce?
dek: The Model Is No Longer the Moat contains two theses: a well-supported scarcity migration toward power, chips, data, and distribution — and a more speculative claim that agent orchestration and harnesses become a durable moat. This follow-up isolates the hinge: if models become commodities, does orchestration remain scarce, or does it become commodity software too?

title: The Model Is No Longer the Moat
dek: Public excerpts attributed to a Dimension Capital August 2026 China memo argue that open-weight models are compressing the intelligence layer. This desk case turns that incomplete public evidence into an investment question: if models become interchangeable, where does economic value migrate — chips, power, data, distribution, or the systems that route, verify, and deploy agents?

title: See’s Candies, 1972: the franchise they almost didn’t buy
dek: Buffett and Munger bought See’s through Blue Chip Stamps at a hard $25 million ceiling. Reconstruct the thesis from filings and letters — pricing power, thin tangible capital, and a near-miss on price — without turning the later cash gusher into a 1972 prophecy.
